description: Real incident: Guest reports AC units 'on' but no air, confirms using the remotes correctly with settings. Root cause was mixed modes (one head on 'heat', others 'cool' + unit at 80F) on Apt 2 (Sunny). Auto-reply must use neutral language ('make sure using the remotes'), use live Kumo status, auto-set all 3 heads to consistent mode (auto/cool at 65), and tell guest what was found + what was fixed.
guestMessage: We have both of the remotes turned on and set to these settings, still no air coming from either unit all night

conversationHistory.body: Hi Jerome, we’re having some issues with the AC units. Both of them say that they’re on, but no air is being blown out.
Good morning, Kathryn, sorry you're having trouble with the AC. Please don't use the Nest thermostat—it doesn't control the AC. Use the heat pump remotes on the wall in each room instead.
We have both of the remotes turned on and set to these settings, still no air coming from either unit all night

Good morning, Kathryn, sorry the AC isn't coming on. Please don't use the Nest thermostat — it doesn't control the AC. Use the heat pump remotes on the wall in each room instead. Let me know the exact settings you're seeing and if there's still no air.

actionTaken.reason: mixed modes or wrong season mode for complaint

heatPumpInfo.suggestedResponseSnippet: Please make sure you are using the heat pump remotes on the wall in each room. Kathryn, I checked the heat pumps for you (room ~79°F). Before, the modes were cool/heat. One (or more) was in the wrong mode for what you need — the system cannot cool and heat at the same time across heads. I've set all the units to auto at 65°F now so it should cool down shortly. You can still adjust with the wall remotes if you want. Let me know in a few minutes if the air is moving and the temperature is improving!

forbiddenPhrases: it doesn't control the AC. Use the heat pump remotes

notes: Exact follow-up from the Kathryn Booker incident (June 2026). The first auto-reply wrongly assumed Nest misuse. Live HeatPumpTool + neutral phrasing + auto-fix of mixed modes is the required behavior. ConversationHistory now includes earlier host 'don't use Nest / use remotes' message (from full thread paste) so the new judge anti-repetition rule (rule 3: do not re-state prior host factual instructions/advice) + ConversationContextTool priorHostHVACAdvice/repeatedInstructionRisk traces are exercised. For this immediate follow-up the neutral 'make sure you are using' + 'I checked/set all/auto at 65/cool down' is still required (improvement over the earlier bad phrasing + adds the live fix value); in later same-thread AC complaints the judge must force removal of any re-duplicated control reminder.
